channel.title: Slow Dispatch — Essays
channel.description: A personal essay blog by Allan Ninal. Writing about systems, trade-offs, and the parts of engineering that don't fit on a slide.

item.title: Measure before you cache
item.description: Every 'make it faster' project I've ever joined has had the same first hour. Here's what I've learned about resisting the urge to add a Redis.

item.title: In praise of boring systems
item.description: The most valuable technology in my last three jobs was Postgres and a queue. Everything else was either a tool or a tax.

item.title: The shape of a good pull request
item.description: I've reviewed about ten thousand PRs. The good ones look almost identical. Here's the shape — what to put in the diff, the description, and what to leave on the floor.

item.title: Types are a conversation, not a contract
item.description: I used to think strong typing was about preventing bugs. Now I think it's about thinking out loud — and the bugs prevented are a side effect.
